title: Claims Against Public Authorities and Inquest Paralegal
description:
Duncan Lewis Solicitors:

Regulated by the Solicitor's Regulation Authority, Duncan Lewis Solicitors was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in the City of London (Fenchurch Street EC3 M), with offices nationwide. We are recognised by the Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners UK independent legal directories as a top-tier law firm in all of our key practice areas - "a diligent and professional team that is prepared to go the extra mile for its clients". A paperless law firm with over 500 personnel that embraces hybrid-working, we service both corporate entities and private individuals in over 25 areas of law across 60 languages. We give people a voice - that is our ethos.

Recognised among The Times 200 Best Law Firms, we have been awarded Law Firm of the Year at the 2024 Lexis Nexis Awards and 2023 Modern Law Awards, reflecting our dedication to legal expertise and client service. We hold Investors in People Gold Standard accreditation for over 15 years, showcasing our commitment to professional development. Duncan Lewis is also Law Society Lexcel, Cyber Essentials Plus, and ISO 27001 certified, ensuring excellence in practice management and data security.

We are committed to recruiting dedicated and talented professionals and welcome applications from exceptional candidates. At Duncan Lewis, we value training and diversity, and we take pride in our inclusive workforce.

About the role:

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking a talented and experienced paralegals to join its Claims Against Public Authorities and Inquest department

The successful candidate will conduct supervised casework and also support other lawyers in the department. You will be involved with case preparation generally and, as part of that role, will be expected to conduct legal research, take proofs of evidence from clients and witnesses, attend both court hearings and conferences

Experience of Legal Aid Agency (LAA) funded casework is highly desirable. Previous CAPA and/or Inquest experience is advantageous.

It is imperative that you can demonstrate an unwavering commitment to protecting individual citizens' civil liberties and a preparedness to fight hard to enforce their human rights. While experience in CAPA work is advantageous, applications from candidates with relevant legal experience and a genuine interest in civil liberties and human rights work will also be considered.

Main Responsibilities of the Role:
- Reporting to Supervising Solicitor and when necessary to Departmental Director
- Working cohesively within a team but also prepared to take responsibility for individual work.
- Attending clients, taking instructions and briefing and liaising with counsel, negotiating with defendant solicitors, the PPO, IOPC and other legal professionals.
- Drafting legal documents.
- Exercising financial control over work carried out, with particular regard to the conversion of work in progress and ensuring that billing targets are met.
- Ensuring Quality Control compliance as defined in the Office Manual in regard to Lexcel, Investors in People and any other quality mark implemented by the firm, dealing with noncompliance matters in an efficient and timely fashion.
- Supporting the successful development of the firm, in line with its Business Plan, this will require participation in marketing events to ensure the continuous growth of the Department, and that the turnover target set for your department is achieved.
- Dealing with any complaints received on your cases.
- Assisting with audit enquiries, when applicable
- Carrying out any other reasonable and relevant task required by Management

Key Skills Required:
- Minimum 1 year of paralegal practice required; experience in a claims against public authorities department is highly desirable.
- Intelligence and demonstrable experience relevant to this role
- Experience working on Legal Aid cases and Litigation is essential (Ideally within Inquests/CAPA)
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage time effectively
- Familiarity with the Legal Aid Agency's online CCMS system would be an advantage
- Legal skills and knowledge, Negotiation skills and Analytical skills
- You must be a good administrator, capable of ordering documents, dealing with new telephone and email enquiries and completing legal aid/controlled work documentation.

What we offer:
- Competitive salary
- The opportunity to join a heavyweight civil liberties firm which promotes a healthy collegiate environment in which to do great work, grow, be supported and be yourself
- Work within a friendly, collaborative and cohesive team
- Excellent progression opportunities
- Support for appropriate legal awards/recognition

The recruitment process will fully comply with GDPR and other applicable laws. Background checks including CRB / DBS checks will establish your eligibility to work in the UK and suitability to the role.

Equal Opportunities:

Duncan Lewis is committed to Equal Opportunities and embraces diversity of its staff. The Company strives to ensure that our staff reflects the diversity of the communities we serve, which is reflective at all levels within our workforce.

We guarantee an interview for candidates that disclose a disability and meet the essential requirements for the post. Please provide additional details in your covering letter if this applies.

APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED BY AGENCIES WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED FOR THE ABOVE VACANCY

title: Data Claims Caseworker Paralegal
description:
Duncan Lewis Solicitors:

Regulated by the Solicitor's Regulation Authority, Duncan Lewis Solicitors was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in the City of London (Fenchurch Street EC3 M), with offices nationwide. We are recognised by the Legal 500 and Chambers & Partners UK independent legal directories as a top-tier law firm in all of our key practice areas - "a diligent and professional team that is prepared to go the extra mile for its clients". A paperless law firm with over 500 personnel that embraces hybrid-working, we service both corporate entities and private individuals in over 25 areas of law across 60 languages. We give people a voice - that is our ethos.

Recognised among The Times 200 Best Law Firms, we have been awarded Law Firm of the Year at the 2024 Lexis Nexis Awards and 2023 Modern Law Awards, reflecting our dedication to legal expertise and client service. We hold Investors in People Gold Standard accreditation for over 15 years, showcasing our commitment to professional development. Duncan Lewis is also Law Society Lexcel, Cyber Essentials Plus, and ISO 27001 certified, ensuring excellence in practice management and data security.

About the Role:

Duncan Lewis Solicitors is seeking a talented and motivated Data Claims Caseworker Paralegal to join its highly regarded Data Claims Department.

The successful candidate will primarily be responsible for the New Client Diary and case set-up/onboarding as well as assistant casework support to the other lawyers in the department. You will be involved with speaking/communicating with new clients and, as part of that role, will be expected to obtain all relevant evidence from them ahead of case opening.

The successful candidate will preferably have prior experience with Data Claims work or at least an interest in data protection, privacy rights as well as unlawful processing/disclosure/retention/misuse of personal data.

Duties and responsibilities
- Reporting directly to the Departmental Director
- Communicating/liaising with new and existing clients by taking initial instructions and obtaining evidence in support of their claims.
- Creating files and preparing all necessary documentation for client onboarding.
- Assisting with casework support from other lawyers in the department.
- Maintaining accurate case records and ensuring compliance with the firm's quality and regulatory standards.
- Managing time recording and file administration effectively.
- Supporting departmental business development and marketing initiatives where required.
- Undertaking any other reasonable duties as directed by Management.

Experience and qualifications
- Minimum one-year of Caseworker Paralegal experience within a law firm/litigation environment.
- Experience with Data Claims work is preferable.
- Interest in dealing with claims involving the UK GDPR 2018, Data Protection Act 2018, privacy rights and misuse of private information is highly desirable.
- Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise tasks and manage time effectively.
- Strong analytical and drafting skills.
- Excellent communication and client care skills.
- Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
- Strong administration and file management skills.
- Experience handling client enquiries, maintaining accurate records and preparing/managing documentation.
- Strong attention to detail and ability to work effectively under pressure.
- Experience using case management systems and Microsoft Office applications.

Benefits

The Company offers competitive salaries and recognises the need to retain and reward its employees through both non-financial lifestyle rewards and financial benefits. The company operates a pay review policy, available to all staff, that sets out clearly salary review procedures available upon meeting performance targets. Our approach to rewards and benefits includes:
- Clear salary review procedures
- Automatic enrolment on to the company's pension scheme.
- 22 days annual leave which increases with length of service
- Additional birthday leave
- 7 days paid occupational sick pay
- Full payment towards annual renewal of Practising Certificate (SRA, CILEX)
- Full payment of Law Society Registration Fee for Panel Membership
- Full payment of Panel membership courses mandatory for Law Society Accreditation
- Individual access to company's e-library resources and training webinar library
- Employee Assistance Programme (EAP)
- Wellbeing support - Mental Health First Aiders available
- Employee Referral/Introduction Scheme
- Eyesight test vouchers
- Maternity gift/vouchers
- Full payment of employment related DBS checks
- Temporary working from abroad (in exceptional circumstances)
- Part-time working considered
- Flexible working arrangements considered, such as Hybrid-Working and Compressed Hours
- Internal training contract intake - apply to train as a solicitor as authorised by the SRA and delivery of training. Successful retention, where appropriate and in accordance with business need, as a newly qualified solicitor
- Support for SQE1 exams
- Clear promotional opportunities (to Supervisor or Director) subject to business needs.
- Company support in becoming more prominent in field of practice through national industry award nominations, national legal directory submissions, media appearances and press releases.
- Enrolment on to Company Medical Cash Plan

subject to terms and conditions.

Company culture

At Duncan Lewis, we are committed to excellence, diversity, and social justice. Our teams work on matters that have a genuine impact on people's lives, often representing vulnerable individuals and holding public bodies to account through expert legal representation.

We foster an inclusive and collaborative working environment where talent is recognised, professional development is encouraged, and employees are supported to achieve their full potential. With award-winning training, clear progression pathways, and a strong commitment to diversity and inclusion, Duncan Lewis offers an exceptional platform for building a successful legal career.

Join a firm where your contribution matters and where you can help give people a voice.

title: Bookkeeper - practice
description:
Bookkeeper

Salary: £30,000 - £35,000 per annum

Location: Langport, Somerset, office based

Job Type: Full-time, Permanent (9am-5:30pm Mon-Thu and 9am-2pm Fri)

A long-established and highly respected accountancy practice based in South Somerset is currently recruiting for a Bookkeeper to join their small team. For over 100 years, the firm has been supporting local businesses, individuals, and entrepreneurs with their accounting, taxation, bookkeeping, and business advisory needs. The practice prides itself on delivering a personal, proactive service and building long-term relationships with clients across a wide range of industries.

The successful candidate will join a friendly and experienced team of accountancy, tax, payroll, and client support professionals, working closely with colleagues to provide exceptional service to a loyal and growing client base.

The Opportunity

This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys building client relationships, working with cloud accounting software, and being part of a supportive and collaborative team environment. You'll become part of a close-knit team that genuinely values client relationships, collaboration, and professional development, whilst enjoying a varied role with responsibility and autonomy from day one

Key Responsibilities
- Maintaining accurate bookkeeping records for a portfolio of clients.
- Processing sales invoices, purchase invoices, receipts, and payments.
- Completing bank reconciliations and investigating discrepancies.
- Preparing and submitting VAT returns.
- Assisting with management accounts preparation.
- Supporting clients with day-to-day accounting queries.
- Working with cloud accounting platforms, including Xero, QuickBooks, and Sage.
- Reviewing bookkeeping records to ensure compliance and accuracy.
- Liaising directly with clients to obtain information and provide support.
- Assisting the wider accounts team with year-end accounting requirements.
- Maintaining strong client relationships and delivering excellent customer service.

Skills & Experience Required
- Previous bookkeeping experience within an accountancy practice or similar environment.
- Good working knowledge of Xero, Sage and/or QuickBooks.
- Experience preparing VAT returns.
- Strong understanding of double-entry bookkeeping principles.
- Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Confident communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to manage multiple deadlines and workloads effectively.
- AAT qualification or equivalent would be advantageous but is not essential.
- Strong IT skills and confidence using cloud-based accounting software.

Salary & Benefits
- £30,000 - £35,000 depending on experience.
- Friendly and supportive team environment.
- Opportunity to work within a well-established and respected local practice, part of a wider group
- Ongoing training and professional development.
- Modern cloud-based systems and technology.
- 22 days holiday + bank hols
- Pension scheme.

title: Payroll Administrator
description:
Payroll Administrator

Location: Yeovil

Salary: £25,000 - £30,000

Hours: Full-time or Part-time (minimum 30 hours per week)

Working Pattern: Office-based during training, with hybrid working available thereafter

Are you an experienced Payroll Administrator looking to join a friendly and supportive accountancy practice where flexibility, professional development and work-life balance are genuinely valued?

Due to continued growth, a well-established accountancy practice in Yeovil is looking to recruit a Payroll Administrator to join its busy payroll department. Working as part of a close-knit team, you'll be responsible for delivering an accurate and efficient payroll service to a diverse client portfolio while enjoying excellent support and development opportunities.

This opportunity would suit someone with previous payroll experience who enjoys building client relationships, working as part of a team and managing a varied workload in a fast-paced practice environment.

The Role

As Payroll Administrator, your responsibilities will include:
- Processing end-to-end payrolls for a portfolio of clients
- Managing weekly, fortnightly, four-weekly and monthly payrolls
- Processing starters, leavers and contractual changes
- Calculating statutory payments including SSP, SMP and SPP
- Managing pension administration and auto-enrolment duties
- Submitting RTI information to HMRC
- Handling payroll queries from clients and employees
- Maintaining accurate payroll records and ensuring compliance with payroll legislation
- Supporting colleagues within the payroll team during busy periods

About You

To be successful in this role, you'll ideally have:
- Previous payroll experience within an accountancy practice, payroll bureau or in-house payroll environment
- Knowledge of current payroll legislation and processes
- Strong attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Excellent organisational and time management skills
- The ability to work effectively to deadlines
- Strong communication and customer service skills
- Experience using payroll software and Microsoft Excel

What's on Offer?

In return, you'll benefit from a supportive and flexible working environment along with an excellent benefits package, including:
- Hybrid working following a successful training and onboarding period
- Flexible working arrangements that can be tailored around personal commitments, including school runs and other family responsibilities
- Full-time or part-time hours available (minimum 30 hours per week)
- 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
- Free on-site parking
- Cycle to Work scheme
- Study support towards professional payroll qualifications, including the Level 3 CIPP qualification
- Regular staff socials and team events
- Friendly and collaborative team environment

Why Join?

This is a fantastic opportunity to join a growing and supportive accountancy practice that genuinely invests in its people. You'll become part of a small team where your contribution is recognised, whilst benefiting from flexible working arrangements, ongoing training and support towards professional payroll qualifications.

If you're looking for a role where you can continue developing your payroll career within a welcoming practice environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply online ASAP, shortlisted applicants will be contacted within 48 working hours.

title: Receptionist / Administrator
description: We are looking for a Receptionist / Administrator to work 25.5 hours per week - for the right candiate we will also train them to work in our dispensary to cover holidays etc. This role is very varied and interesting.
